question: Without ranking from filenames, what do inventoried permit documents establish, and which document governs if they disagree?

judgment.semantic_question_used: Are narrative permit-package document conditions available as workspace evidence for purposes B and C beyond document_inventory.json metadata alone?
judgment.interpretation: The unresolved claim that permit document text is unavailable is falsified by workspace evidence. sources/document_inventory.json inventories 12 permit-package documents by filename, hash, permit number, document kind, and byte size only—it carries no narrative text. However, PASS_TASK.md and documents/INDEX.md establish that permit-package text extracts under documents/ are authoritative sources. All 12 inventoried documents have corresponding .txt extracts (matching facility and document_kind) containing full narrative permit conditions: effluent limitations, monitoring frequencies, discharge authorizations, and interpretive footnotes (e.g., conditional 'When discharging' monitoring). Narrative permit text is therefore available in the workspace for purposes B and C, even though it is not embedded in the structured document_inventory.json table.
judgment.grounding: document_inventory.json lists 12 documents with metadata fields (path, filename, document_kind, permit, bytes, sha256, origin) and no text content. documents/INDEX.md catalogs 12 permit-package text extracts whose facility and document_kind values correspond one-to-one to the inventory entries. Sampled text files (e.g., documents/aztec/final_permit.txt, documents/farmington/final_permit.txt) contain narrative permit conditions including monitoring requirements and footnotes that address the kinds of conditional and aggregated obligations flagged elsewhere in construction.py for purposes B and C.
